caseno: CRIMINAL PETITION FOR LEAVE TO APPEAL NO. 153 OF 2002
lawyer: For the Petitioners: Mr. Muhammad Roushan Ali,  Senior Advocate, Instructed by Mr. Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-record. Respondents: Not Represented.
parties:
Md. Farid Miah Chowdhury------Petitioner
Versus
Mrs. Jahanara Begum and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. M. M. Ruhul Amin, J.:- This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 16.07.2002 passed by a Division bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4188 of 2000 discharging the rule. 

 2. Short facts are that the Petitioner's daughter Nasreen Akter was married to accused respondent Abdul Monaf. On demand of dowry the petitioner constructed a dwelling but in the house of his son-in-law at his village home. Inspite of the same the accused persons demanded dowry of Tic 20,000/- from him. When he refused to pay the said amount the accused person conjointly assaulted his daughter and killed her and thrown her dead body on the rail-way line and circulated that she committed suicide. The respondent informed the matter to the local police station, upon which U.D. Case No. 10 of 1997 was started. Police after investigation submitted final report stating that the victim committed suicide. The learned Magistrate accepted the final report. The learned Magistrate while accepting the final report considered the inquest report of the dead body, post-mortem report and the opinion of the doctor to the effect that the death of the deceased was due to shock and hemorrhage resulting from injuries which were ante mortem and accidental in nature. Thereafter, the petitioner preferred Criminal Revision No. 406 of 1998 before the High Court Division and by order dated 18.03.1999 the Rule was made absolute and the learned Magistrate was directed to ask the officer-in-charge of the local police station to submit police report informing the Magistrate as to the result and the action taken upon the petition of complaint. On receipt of this order of the High Court Division the learned Magistrate directed the officer-in-charge, Laksham Police Station to submit the report in pursuance of the observation of the High Court Division. The officer-in-charge of Laksham Police Station again submitted the report. Thereafter The Criminal Investigation Department took up investigation of the case with the approval of the court and after holding investigation again submitted final report. During investigation by C.I.D. the present petitioner was examined but in support of his claim he did not produce any witness to the investigating officer of Criminal Investigation Department. During investigation by Criminal Investigation Department is transpired that alleged victim Nasreen Akhter fell in love with one Rafiqul Islam with whom she eloped and they were caught in the waiting room of Laksham Railway Station and they were brought to the house of Arab Ali, father of the accused No. I and lastly she was married to accused No.1 Monaf, as Rafiqul Islam abandoned her and it further transpired that the deceased was a woman of questionable character and the petitioner had no social connection with his daughter after the incident of her elopement and marriage with the respondent No. 1 . The petitioner then filed a Naraji petition. The learned Magistrate sent the case record along with final report submitted by the investigation officer of Criminal Investigation Department to the Court of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjratan Bishesh Adalat, Comilla as the learned Magistrate had no jurisdiction to take cognizance in this case. The learned Judge of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat after hearing the parties and on perusal of the relevant papers and documents rejected the Naraji petition filed by the petitioner and accepted the final report. 

 4. It is on record that the case was twice investigated once by the local police and then by the Criminal Investigation Department and the investigation officers took into consideration the post-mortem report wherein Medical Officer opined that the death of the deceased was accidental and also the fact that the petitioner did not adduce any evidence before the investigating officer or the Criminal Investigation Department and also the other facts and circumstances of the case. The High Court Division it appears found that the Naraji petition of the petitioner was not supported by any materials. The High Court Division accordingly on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and relevant materials on record rejected the naraji petition. 

 5. In our view, the High Court Division in the facts and circumstances of the case as stated above committed no illegality in passing the impugned order rejecting the naraji petition and accepting the police report submitted by investigating officer of the Criminal Investigation Department. 6. Accordingly, this petition is dismissed.
